brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Quillnest, the writing app in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: encouraging and a little bold, for 13–17 year-olds, never childish or school-like. No owls, no pencils or quills drawn literally, no lightbulbs, no speech bubbles. App icon for iOS and Android plus a web version.

claim.notes: All three concepts (next-step, growing-rings, q-caret) failed the critic's quality gate after two rounds (best average 6.2, distinctiveness 4–5), so nothing was finalized, exported or put in the gallery.

concepts.title: First Loop
readsAs: a magnifying-glass search icon (ring plus handle), strongest in the 16 px tab
an eye or fried egg with a coral yolk. Unfortunate: a search/find app icon
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a target or spiral, close to an @ or a loading spinner at 16 px, struck as generic; s2 a spiral or record/loading icon, struck; s3 a lowercase n or an arched doorway, a different letter, struck; s4 a figure with arms raised or a dot rising out of a bowl or sunrise, the 'just hatched' idea comes through; s5 an eclipse or crescent moon with a dot, 0.89 stock shape, struck. Keep s4: it is the only one where something is happening (a lift-off) and it is encouraging without being childish. Risks to fix: (1) the 'person with arms up' reading is the stock wellness/community/meditation logo, so push away from a human figure (break the symmetry, give the dot a direction or offset, make the bowls feel like a nest and not a smile); (2) at 16 px the two thin bowls merge into a smiley or Wi-Fi signal, so thicken the strokes or reduce to one bold bowl; (3) the dot must not read as a notification badge; (4) coral plus blue is fine for the brief, keep away from teal.

concepts.title: Next Step
readsAs: speed stripes / sportswear or motorsport slashes
a '//' code-comment or URL slash. Unfortunate: an energy-drink or racing brand, nothing about writing or encouragement
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 two offset tiles, purple low and gold jumped up; the hook (next step, one rung higher) lands. s2 one tile sliced and bumped, a cut tile that also reads as a 'compare' or 'split view' UI icon, struck. s3 a staircase with a floating pill; the gold pill reads as a notification badge at 16 px and stairs-to-success is the growth cliche, struck. s4 stair-line plus gold dot: a staircase or a Z/lightning bolt at 16 px, and the dot sits exactly where an unread badge goes, struck. Keep s1: the jump is bold and not school-like. Fix: (1) the gold tile's huge single rounded corner reads as a speech-bubble or leaf tab, and speech bubbles are banned, so give both tiles one consistent corner logic; (2) two loose squares is stock geometry, so make the relationship ownable (a shared edge, a lift that shows momentum, a proportion change) rather than two floating blocks; (3) avoid a podium or bar-chart reading; (4) check the gold block never reads as a badge in the corner of an app icon.

concepts.title: Q Caret
readsAs: a geometric Q built from a disc with a notched-out corner and a lifted red tab
a Pac-Man / pie chart with a slice removed
a red correction tag or eraser. Unfortunate: teacher's red-pen mark, school grading
concepts.sketchNotes: Second review (rebuilt board, no Q, no cursor). Reads as: s1 a dark tile sliced on a diagonal with the top half knocked up in lime; this is a cut block with a lifted piece, the same move as the developed next-step concept (notched dark block plus lifted gold piece) and 0.74 stock shape, so struck as too close and generic. s2 three stacked bars: a text-align or hamburger-menu icon, and lines of text are the product's own object drawn plainly, struck. s4 a page with a folded corner: the document icon, an explicit cliche, struck. s3 a lime slash standing on a dark baseline; first reading is an angle sign or a '/_' code glyph, second a stroke hitting a line. Only s3 survives and it stays clearly apart from next-step. Keep the single bold diagonal against the flat baseline. Fix: (1) make the contact the event, with the slash touching or denting the line rather than floating above it, so it reads as a landing and not as a typographic symbol; (2) avoid the lime bar reading as a highlighter or pencil, so use no rounded tip and no taper toward a point; (3) work the proportions (slash weight, line length, angle) until it stops looking like a math or code glyph at 16 px; (4) black plus acid lime reads bold and grown-up, so keep it.
